statement: By the time a06 ran, crates/enforcer-domain/src/ids.rs already fully defined HubName and LaneId as branded newtypes (private inner String, parse-at-boundary TryFrom<String>/FromStr, serde try_from/into wiring, Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq/Hash/PartialOrd/Ord/Display derives) with filesystem-safe charset validation (lowercase alnum + '-' for HubName, + '_' for LaneId; no path separators or '.' in either allow-list, so '..' escapes and '/'/'\\' are structurally impossible, not merely denylisted). crates/enforcer-coordination/src/{api.rs,domain.rs} already consumed &HubName/&LaneId exclusively in every public signature (init, claim_all, release, closeout, stream_path, lock_path, WriterId::new) -- never a bare String -- and domain.rs's own module doc already states HubName/LaneId are 're-used from enforcer-domain ... rather than re-declared'.
why: The a06 workpack's owns line (crates/enforcer-domain/src/coordination_ids.rs) and prose ('populates the enforcer-domain crate') read as if the newtypes did not exist yet, but a05-adjacent work had already landed them in ids.rs under a different filename. Creating a separate coordination_ids.rs would have duplicated/shadowed the already-adopted types and broken enforcer-coordination's existing imports.
howToApply: Before creating a workpack's named 'owns' file, grep the crate for the type names the workpack is about to define; if they already exist under a different filename and are already consumed by dependent crates, EXTEND the existing file in place and do not create the named file -- the file path in a workpack's 'owns' line is aspirational, not authoritative, when it predates the actual implementation.

statement: Extended crates/enforcer-domain/src/ids.rs in place (no new file) with: doc comments on HubName/LaneId documenting the compile-time nominal-distinctness guarantee and citing enforcer-coordination's adoption; a coordination_id_brand_decode test matching TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md row a06's named oracle, covering empty/unsafe-charset (including '../escape', 'a/b', 'a\\b')/oversize (129 chars for HubName's 128 bound, 65 for LaneId's 64 bound) rejection plus a serde-boundary check; and a hub_name_and_lane_id_are_not_interchangeable test as the 'compile-reject fixture' -- two helper fns each typed to accept only their own branded type, proving by the module's own successful compilation that a LaneId cannot be substituted for a HubName (no trybuild dependency exists anywhere in this workspace's Cargo.lock, and a03/a04/a05's own Sha256/RuleId newtypes follow the same no-trybuild, type-signature-is-the-proof pattern).
why: TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md row a06 (PENDING at start of this lane) names 'coordination-id-brand-decode + compile-reject fixture' as the required proof; since the newtypes already existed and satisfied every functional acceptance-checklist item, the only real work was closing this named-proof gap without inventing a new test-framework dependency the rest of the a0x series does not use.
howToApply: For any future ax0 'compile-reject fixture' proof row in this workspace, follow the established convention: two or more monomorphic helper functions parameterized on the specific branded type, called only with matching types in the test body, with a comment noting the swapped-argument variant would not compile -- do not add trybuild or any other new dev-dependency for this.

statement: crates/enforcer-coordination/src/domain.rs's resolve_ledger_root/ledger_home take hub_override: Option<&str> and env-var strings (OCENTRA_COORDINATION_HUB / OCENTRA_ENFORCER_HUB) and join them into a filesystem path via ledger_home().join(hub) WITHOUT parsing through HubName first -- this is a real gap against a06's 'path construction consumes only these newtypes' intent, but it lives in enforcer-coordination (not enforcer-domain) and so is out of a06's owned scope (crates/enforcer-domain/src/coordination_ids.rs only; the gate commands are scoped to -p enforcer-domain).
why: Flagging this now so a future enforcer-coordination-owning lane (arc-16 or a coordination-specific workpack) closes it rather than it being silently missed: no other crate in the workspace currently calls resolve_ledger_root (grep for callers returned zero matches outside its own module), so this is not yet a live cross-crate risk, but it is the one place left where a raw hub string reaches path construction.
howToApply: A future lane touching crates/enforcer-coordination/src/domain.rs should change resolve_ledger_root's hub_override parameter to Option<&HubName> (or parse the env-var string through HubName::from_str before the .join call) to close this out; do not silently leave it since it is the one path-construction call site a06's own acceptance checklist explicitly calls for.
